questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech. "I live in Mumbai," she said.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

"I live in Mumbai," she said.

options.text: She said that she has been living in Mumbai.
options.html: She said that she has been living in Mumbai.

options.text: She said that she had been living in Mumbai.
options.html: She said that she had been living in Mumbai.

options.text: She said that she lived in Mumbai.
options.html: She said that she lived in Mumbai.

options.text: She says that she was living in Mumbai.
options.html: She says that she was living in Mumbai.

questions.solution:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Simple Present Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Simple Past Tense.

Simple Present (Subject + V1 + Object) should be converted into Simple Past (Subject + V2 + Object).

"That" is used in place of Inverted Commas while transforming the sentence from Direct Speech to Indirect Speech.

For example:

He said, "I never go to the village." (Direct Speech)

He said that he never went to the village. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· Inverted commas ("...") are replaced with 'that'.

· The verb 'live' (simple present) is changed into 'lived' (simple past).

· The pronoun 'I' is changed into 'she'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: She said that she lived in Mumbai.

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. "Buy sweet apples, or none at all", he instructed his servant. B. A rich man sent his servant to an orchard to buy some apples. C. The servant asked, "How am I to know that all of them are sweet if I taste just one?" D. The owner of the orchard said to the servant, "All my apples are sweet. Try one."
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. "Buy sweet apples, or none at all", he instructed his servant.

B. A rich man sent his servant to an orchard to buy some apples.

C. The servant asked, "How am I to know that all of them are sweet if I taste just one?"

D. The owner of the orchard said to the servant, "All my apples are sweet. Try one."
questions.solution:
Sentence B comes first as it provides a platform to carry forward the story. B states that a rich man sent his servant to buy some apples. A follows B as it talks about the rich man's instruction. So, BA is a pair. D and C are the conversations between the owner of the shop and the servant. In sentence D the owner said to the servant to try one so that the servant can find out whether the apple is sweet or not. C follows D as it is the response of the servant. Therefore, BADC becomes the correct order among the given options.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Richard wore a broad belt with shiny buckles.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Richard wore a broad belt with shiny buckles.

options.text: A broad belt with shiny buckles was worn by Richard.
options.html: A broad belt with shiny buckles was worn by Richard.

options.text: A broad belt with shiny buckles had been worn by Richard.
options.html: A broad belt with shiny buckles had been worn by Richard.

options.text: A broad belt with shiny buckles wore Richard.
options.html: A broad belt with shiny buckles wore Richard.

options.text: A broad belt with shiny buckles was wear by Richard.
options.html: A broad belt with shiny buckles was wear by Richard.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Past Indefinite. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Past Indefinite.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + V2 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Real Madrid won the Champions League. (Active Voice)

The Champions League was won by Real Madrid. (Passive Voice)

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: A broad belt with shiny buckles was worn by Richard.
